CONGRANT.TITLE: CREST Center for Multidisciplinary Research Excellence in Cyber-Physical Infrastructure Systems (MECIS)
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
Overview:
The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) proposes to establish the “CREST Center for Multidisciplinary Research Excellence in Cyber-Physical Infrastructure Systems (MECIS).” The Center’s mission is to advance and transform the much-needed research and education at the nexus of automation, sensors, and artificial intelligence (AI), as integral parts of the “NSF’s 10 Big Ideas,” anticipating the revolutionary cyber-physical infrastructure systems (CIS). Three Colleges of Engineering, Sciences, and Education at UTRGV in collaboration with the Universities of Illinois (at Urbana-Champaign and at Chicago) and California (Riverside) will pursue multidisciplinary research on CIS, aiming to: (i) transfer technology to various transportation, logistics, manufacturing, and construction industries; and (ii) prepare a minority STEM workforce to drive future CIS-based communities. The Center envisions a portfolio of three research subprojects on automation, sensors, and AI that bridges diverse STEM disciplines. A holistic, multi-level approach is adopted to address CIS planning, design, and operation. While each subproject constitutes a unique element, their synergy ensures the CIS integrity.
Subproject 1 pushes the frontiers of knowledge in future transportation infrastructure, which will be transformed by autonomous vehicles (AVs) and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), in six directions: (i) at the planning level, public acceptance and policy issues of (U)AV; (ii-iv) at the design level, computer vision, automatic navigation, and model/field-based testing of the designed capabilities; and (v, vi) at the operation level, human-(U)AV interactions and network-wide inter-(U)AV interactions.
Subproject 2 designs and embeds sensors in CIS for two purposes. First, (U)AV sensors help perform automated tasks. Second, sensors in civil infrastructure and (U)AVs monitor infrastructure health. Three research areas are defined: (i, ii) at the design level, computational simulation, synthesis, and 3D printing of sensor materials and UAV structures, and (iii) at the operation level, cost-effective decision-making to upkeep infrastructure health using sensor data.
Since (U)AVs and sensors will inherently generate big data, Subproject 3 will synchronously work with subprojects 1 and 2 to: (i) develop AI solutions for big data management, and (ii) develop AI algorithms for big data analytics and decision making in the design and operation of (U)AVs and infrastructure.
UTRGV is the nation’s second largest Hispanic-Serving Institute (HIS) located in South Texas with an established record of preparing underrepresented minority students for STEM careers. The Center will provide (under)graduate students with cutting-edge CIS research experience, will integrate CIS research and education, and will pave a pathway from High School through graduate programs in STEM disciplines. This broad initiative at UTRGV will also offer new courses related to the subprojects. The Center will further enhance the research infrastructure at UTRGV and will strengthen the research competitiveness of a diverse group of faculty.
Intellectual Merit:
The proposed self-sustaining Center will play a key role in transforming the scientific discoveries at the intersection of automation, sensors, and AI technologies, which are the integral elements of next-generation CIS. The Center will address current gaps in the planning, design, and operation of CIS by proposing innovative theoretical, computational, experimental, and empirical solutions spanning from micro (molecule)- to macro (system)-scale, which also yield practical solutions valuable for the industry.
Broader Impacts:
The Center’s research and education activities will develop an underrepresented workforce equipped with the skills to address complex societal problems. The Center will partner with the public and private sectors to advance technology transfer and product development in CIS. The Center’s activities are key for the establishment of an inaugural engineering doctoral program, which will be vital in elevating UTRGV to a Research I institution and advancing the CIS research agenda in a predominantly HSI. The Center's research findings will be made available to the research community as journal publications and conference proceedings, which will inform other domains undergoing related transformations, such as the health industry, manufacturing and production systems, and the military.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Distributed Control of Uncertain Systems
CONGRANT.AWARDORG: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: Overview:Distributed cooperative control of multiple systems plays an important role in many civilian and military applications where cooperation of multiple systems need work cooperatively. However,distributed controller design is challenging because 1) for each system the available information is the states/outputs of its own and its neighbors and 2) each system may be nonlinear and has un-certainty. In order to solve this challenging control problem, the following three research problems are proposed in this proposal: 1) distributed output tracking control of multiple heterogeneous un-certain linear systems, 2) distributed output tracking control of multiple heterogeneous nonlinear systems, and 3) distributed output tracking control of multiple heterogeneous uncertain nonlinear systems. To solve the above three research problems, a general multiple-step distributed immersion and invariance controller design (DIICD) approach and a distributed virtual-system tracking con-troller design (DVSTCD) approach will be proposed. Then, it is proposed to study how to solve each research problem with the aid of the DIICD approach and the DVSTCD approach with the aid of other techniques. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed research results, experimental study will be conducted by implementing the proposed control laws in the multi-robot testbed in the PI's research laboratory. Based on the experimental results, the proposed distributed control laws will be improved accordingly.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Distributed Leader-Following Tracking Control of Heterogeneous Uncertain Systems: A Distributed Immersion and Invariance Approach
Distributed Leader-Following Tracking Control of Heterogeneous Uncertain Systems: A Distributed Immersion and Invariance Approach
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
Distributed output tracking control of multiple systems plays an important role in many civilian
and military applications where cooperation of multiple systems need work cooperatively. However,
distributed controller design is challenging because 1) for each system the available information is
the states/outputs of its own and its neighbors and 2) each system may be nonlinear and has uncertainty.
In order to solve this challenging control problem, the following three research problems are
proposed to be studied in this proposal: 1) distributed output tracking control of multiple heterogeneous
uncertain linear systems, 2) distributed output tracking control of multiple heterogeneous
nonlinear systems, and 3) distributed output tracking control of multiple heterogeneous uncertain
nonlinear systems. To solve the above three research problems, a general multiple-step distributed
immersion and invariance controller design (DIICD) approach will be proposed. Then, it is proposed
to study how to solve each research problem with the aid of the proposed DIICD approach
and other techniques. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed research results, experimental
study will be conducted by implementing the proposed control laws in the multi-robot testbed in
the PI's research laboratory. Based on the experimental results, the proposed distributed control
laws will be improved accordingly.

Intellectual Merit:
The cooperative control of multiple identical linear systems has been extensively studied in
the past decade and fruitful results have been obtained. However, these results cannot be applied
to solve the leader-following tracking problem of multiple heterogeneous uncertain systems with
limited information of its neighbors. This project will solve the leader-following tracking control
problems of multiple heterogeneous systems with different assumptions on the dynamics and uncertainty
in each system. The intellectual merits of this proposal are as follows: 1. a novel distributed
immersion and invariance controller design approach is proposed for the leader-following tracking
control problem; 2. the leader-following tracking control problem of multiple heterogeneous
uncertain linear systems is solved; 3. the leader-following tracking control problems of multiple
heterogeneous nonlinear systems with/without uncertainty are solved; and 4. the proposed controller
design procedures can be applied to the distributed cooperative control problems of many
practical control problems, such as 
flocking of mobile robots, formation control of unmanned aerial vehicles, etc.

Broader Impacts:
The research has significant impact in civilian, homeland security, and military applications
where multiple systems work cooperatively. The research also has impact on the fields of biology,
economics, physics, and computer science. The research plan will be integrated into an education
plan including 1) undergraduate and graduate education. The University of Texas Rio Grande
Valley (UTRGV) is a predominantly Hispanic institute. The PI will mentor minority students and
female students through his research. The PI will develop a graduate course and an undergraduate
course which are related to this project; and 2) broader dissemination of the research results. The
research results will be published in journals and conference proceedings. The PI will also work
closely with his industrial partners to transfer research results.

CONGRANT.TITLE: A Smart Campus Testbed (Internal PreProposal for NSF MRI)
CONGRANT.AWARDORG: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
The Internet of Things (IoT) is an emerging area that has a big potential of greatly improving the efficiency of our society and also greatly facilitating the daily life of everyone, particularly the seniors and the disabled [7]. However, the implementation and deployment of IoT has been slow. One main reason is that there is a lack of experimental studies on how the heterogeneous IoT elements in reality would interact and interfere with each other in terms of communications, data sharing, and data use [6]. We propose to build an IoT testbed on the UT-RGV campus to do such studies and thus catalyze the acceptance and adoption of IoT by our community and the society. One of UT-RGV’s goals is to broaden our connections to the local communities. The proposed IoT testbed will contribute to achieving that goal because the testbed will attract the attention and
interest of public administrators, teachers, and the general public. The proposed testbed also meets the intellectual merit and the broader impact requirements of NSF, as detailed later.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Research and Development of Objective Evaluation of Colorized Night-Vision Images
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
In this contractual project, an objective metric (measurement) is expected to evaluate
how much a colorized night-vision picture resembling a daylight color picture (taken by a
digital camera). A set of computer colorized images and their corresponding daylight
pictures will be provided by ASU. The developed method should evaluate how closely
related between a colorized image and a daylight picture. The developed method should
also distinguish the difference among multiple versions of colorized images by telling
which one is better. The objective evaluation results by the proposed method/algorithm
will be compared with the subjective evaluation results by human observers.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: The Effect of Training Dataset Size on SAR Automatic Target Recognition Using Deep Learning
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Proceedings of IEEE 12th International Conference on Electronics Information and Emergency Communication
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is an effective remote sensor for target detection and recognition. Deep learning has a great potential for implementing automatic target recognition based on SAR images. In general, Sufficient labeled data are required to train a deep neural network to avoid overfitting. However, the availability of measured SAR images is usually limited due to high cost and security in practice. In this paper, we will investigate the relationship between the recognition performance and training dataset size. The experiments are performed on three classifiers using MSTAR (Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition) dataset. The results show us the minimum size of the training set for a particular classification accuracy.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Tracking Control of UAVs with Uncertainty and Input Constraints
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: This paper considers the position and attitude tracking control problem of a vertical take-off and landing unmanned aerial vehicle with uncertainty and input constraints. Considering the parametric and non-parametric uncertainties in the dynamics of systems, a robust adaptive tracking controller is proposed with the aid of the special structure of the dynamics of the system. Considering the uncertainty and input constraints, a robust adaptive saturation controller is proposed with the aid of an auxiliary compensated system. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Distributed Robust Formation Flying and Attitude Synchronization of Spacecraft
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: This paper considers the spacecraft formation flying (SFF) with a desired attitude. Two control problems are studied. One is the formation control of multiple spacecraft and the other is the attitude synchronization of multiple spacecraft. To solve the two problems, a 6-DOF model is adopted for each spacecraft. In the 6-DOF model, it is assumed that the inertia parameters are not well known and there are perturbations of orbitals, gravity, etc. With the aid of the backstepping technique and the algebraic graph theory, distributed robust control laws are proposed for the formation flying and attitude synchronization problems, respectively. The effectiveness of the proposed controllers is shown by simulation.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Tracking control of vertical taking-off and landing vehicles with parametric uncertainty
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: International Journal of Adaptive Control and Signal Processing
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Summary This paper considers the position and attitude tracking control of a quadrotor with inertia parameter uncertainty. With the aid of the cascade structure of the dynamics of the system, an immersion and invariance observer is proposed to estimate the unknown mass of the system first. Secondly, a saturation controller is designed for the thrust force. Thirdly, a virtual controller is proposed for the angular velocity of the quadrotor with the aid of a nonlinear transform of the Euler angles. Finally, adaptive and robust controllers are proposed for the torque input of the quadrotor to deal with the unknown inertia moment of the system. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.
